terms.meaning: The side opposite the right angle in a right triangle. It is the longest side.
In a right triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
Three counting numbers a, b, c with a² + b² = c². They can be the sides of a right triangle.
A Baudhayana triple with no common factor greater than 1, such as 3, 4, 5.

items.name: Finding a shorter side
items.example: Hypotenuse 13 and side 5: b² = 169 − 25 = 144, so b = 12.

items.name: Testing for a right angle
items.formula: Check if the two smaller squares add up to the largest
items.example: 7, 24, 25: 49 + 576 = 625, so it is a right triangle.

items.name: Doubling a square
items.formula: Square on the diagonal = 2 × the area
items.example: Side 3: area 9. The square on its diagonal has area 18.

items.name: Halving a square
items.formula: Join the midpoints of the sides
items.example: A square of area 16 gives an inner square of area 8.

items.name: Isosceles right triangle
items.example: Equal sides of 5: c² = 25 + 25 = 50, so c = 5√2.

items.name: Making more triples
items.formula: Multiply all three numbers by the same number

items.name: Diagonal of a rectangle
items.example: Sides 8 cm and 15 cm: d² = 64 + 225 = 289, so d = 17 cm.

items.name: Side of a rhombus
items.formula: Half of each diagonal makes a right triangle

mistakes.text: Add the squares, not the sides. Sides 3 and 4 give hypotenuse 5, not 7.
Do not forget the square root at the end. If c² = 100, then c = 10, not 100.
To find a shorter side, subtract from the square of the hypotenuse. Do not add.
The theorem is only for right triangles. Sides 4, 5, 6 do not fit: 16 + 25 = 41, not 36.
